symbols.name: \mathbb B
symbols.def: The binary alphabet used for observed variables and switch modes.

symbols.name: W
symbols.type: finite set of observed proxy variables
symbols.role: Eligible intervention vertices.

symbols.name: T
symbols.role: Singleton treatment terminal.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.role: Singleton outcome terminal.

symbols.name: R
symbols.role: Independent local mode coordinates.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: The realized assignment of prespecified exogenous device or site configuration bits recorded by the acquisition protocol; it is not inferred from the observed source laws or from latent confounding.

symbols.name: h^*
symbols.role: A completion whose bidirected edge set contains every other completion edge set, when such a completion exists.

symbols.name: E^{\mathrm{fix}}
symbols.role: Bidirected edges present in every completion.

symbols.name: E^{\cup}
symbols.role: The union of the local bidirected switch ports.

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: If \(\lambda(e)=(r,s)\), edge \(e\) is present exactly when \(h_r=s\); repeated coordinates implement equality copies and opposite signs implement complement copies.

symbols.name: \mathcal R_{\lambda}
symbols.def: For guarded edges \(e,e'\in E^{\cup}\), \(e\mathrel{\mathcal R_{\lambda}^{=}}e'\) when \(\lambda(e)=(r,s)\) and \(\lambda(e')=(r,s)\), and \(e\mathrel{\mathcal R_{\lambda}^{\neg}}e'\) when \(\lambda(e)=(r,s)\) and \(\lambda(e')=(r,-s)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.role: A model whose observed graph is the fixed realized completion \(G_h\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The distribution on \(V\) induced by \(\mathcal M\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.role: Unit-cost intervention budget.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Every eligible proxy has unit acquisition cost.

symbols.name: J
symbols.role: A set selected before the exogenous switch record is released.

symbols.name: \mathcal S_J
symbols.role: The observational law and all cells of one complete joint-intervention source.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{h,J}
symbols.role: The logged configuration record released after acquisition, together with the acquired multiplex source used at evaluation time.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)
symbols.role: The positive binary source laws compatible with the fixed graph completion determined by the logged configuration \(h\) under the prespecified guard map.

symbols.name: H_h-J
symbols.def: The graph on \(V\setminus J\) with edge set \(E_h^{\leftrightarrow}\) after deleting \(J\) and its incident edges.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The number of internal proxy vertices on \(\pi\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{1,\pi}
symbols.role: The first member of the positive binary path countermodel pair.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{2,\pi}
symbols.role: The second member of the positive binary path countermodel pair.

symbols.name: \mathcal J_B
symbols.role: Budget-feasible proxy sets that identify the target in every fixed-completion fiber after its exogenous configuration record is released.

symbols.name: \mathbf i
symbols.def: The canonical length-prefixed bit-string encoding of \((V,W,T,Y,E^{\mathrm{fix}},E^{\cup},R,\lambda,\mathcal R_{\lambda},c,B)\): vertices and switches receive consecutive binary indices, vertex and edge sets are sorted index lists, each guard row records an edge index, a switch index, and one sign bit, \(\mathcal R_{\lambda}\) is an encoded equal-or-complement pair table, the cost block records one for every proxy, terminal indices are explicit, and \(B\) is in ordinary binary.

symbols.name: \mathsf{RSJID}
symbols.role: The set of valid binary encodings that admit a budget-feasible proxy set accepted for every switch record.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Ver}
symbols.role: The polynomial predicate used under the universal completion quantifier, with a residual path returned when it rejects.

symbols.name: X
symbols.type: finite set of existential Boolean variables
symbols.role: Outer variables in the quantified reduction.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.type: finite set of universal Boolean variables
symbols.role: Completion variables in the quantified reduction.

symbols.name: \Phi
symbols.def: A formula in the standard true \(\exists X\,\forall Z\) problem.

symbols.name: \mathcal C
symbols.role: The occurrence-copy, consistency-test, clause-chain, and selector-isolation construction.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.role: Maps any budget-feasible cut in a compiled instance to an existential occurrence-copy choice without increasing cardinality.

symbols.name: d
symbols.role: A bound on the completion-wise bidirected degree of both terminals \(T\) and \(Y\).

assumptions.condition: For the fixed completion \(h\), \(\mathcal M\) is recursive and semi-Markovian with observed ADMG \(G_h\).
Every distribution in \(\mathcal S_J\) is induced by the same structural causal model \(\mathcal M\) under the indicated surgical intervention.
The metadata record \(h\) is the logged realization of prespecified exogenous device or site configuration bits whose known guard map \(\lambda\) determines \(G_h\).

novel.justification: Logged hardware modes, laboratory routing settings, and site-administration configurations provide concrete examples in which the mode bits are fixed outside the outcome system and recorded directly.

assumptions.condition: The protocol order is selection of \(J\), acquisition of \(\mathcal S_J\), release of the record \(h\), and evaluation of \(\theta_t(y)\).

novel.justification: A preregistered acquisition followed by release of an already logged configuration file is a realistic administrative sequence for multisite studies and configurable measurement systems.

definitions.name: Positive binary fixed-completion causal-star fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)=\{(\mathcal M,P,\{Q_{J,j}:j\in\mathbb B^J\}):\mathcal M\text{ is recursive semi-Markovian with observed ADMG }G_h,\ P\text{ is strictly positive, all sources share }\mathcal M,\text{ and the logged exogenous record }h\text{ determines }G_h\text{ through }\lambda\}\) for each fixed \(h\in\mathbb B^R\) and \(J\subseteq W\); evaluation uses \(\mathcal I_{h,J}=(h,\mathcal S_J)\).

definitions.name: Robust feasible proxy sets
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal J_B(\mathfrak G)=\{J\subseteq W:\sum_{w\in J}c(w)\le B\text{ and, for every }h\in\mathbb B^R,\ \theta_t(y)\text{ is identifiable from }\mathcal I_{h,J}\text{ over }\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\}\), where acquisition precedes release of the logged configuration record.

definitions.name: Robust star joint-intervention design language
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{RSJID}=\{\mathbf i\in\{0,1\}^*: \mathbf i\text{ decodes to }(V,W,T,Y,E^{\mathrm{fix}},E^{\cup},R,\lambda,\mathcal R_{\lambda},c,B)\text{ and }\exists J\subseteq W\ [\sum_{w\in J}c(w)\le B\ \wedge\ \forall h\in\mathbb B^R,\ \mathsf{Ver}(\mathbf i,J,h)=1]\}\). A valid encoding uses labeled finite sets with \(V=W\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{T,Y\}\), derives \(E^{\to}=\{w\to T:w\in W\}\cup\{T\to Y\}\), lists simple disjoint bidirected sets \(E^{\mathrm{fix}}\) and \(E^{\cup}\), lists \(R\) and the total guard table \(\lambda:E^{\cup}\to R\times\mathbb B\), checks that \(\mathcal R_{\lambda}\) is exactly the induced equality-or-complement relation, records \(c(w)=1\) for every \(w\), names singleton terminals \(T,Y\), and gives \(B\) in binary. The promised hardness sublanguage additionally bounds each switch guard list by an encoding-independent constant and every nonterminal completion-wise bidirected degree by eight; terminal degrees are unrestricted. Malformed strings are outside the language.

definitions.name: Polynomial fixed-completion separation verifier
definitions.construction: On input \(\mathbf i,J,h\), parse and validate the encoded causal-star instance, reject unless \(J\subseteq W\), \(\sum_{w\in J}c(w)\le B\), and \(h\in\mathbb B^R\), construct \(E_h^{\leftrightarrow}=E^{\mathrm{fix}}\cup\{e\in E^{\cup}:\lambda(e)=(r,s),\ h_r=s\}\), and run breadth-first search in \(H_h-J\). Set \(\mathsf{Ver}(\mathbf i,J,h)=1\) exactly when \(Y\) is unreachable from \(T\); when it returns zero after a valid parse, return the predecessor-chain simple \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path as the failure witness.

definitions.name: Positive binary fixed-completion path countermodel pair
definitions.construction: For a fixed \(h\), \(J\), and simple residual path \(\pi=(T,A_1,\ldots,A_k,Y)\), take independent fair \(U_0,\ldots,U_k\in\mathbb B\), set \(c_k=2^{-k}\) and \(b=1/2\), and use \(P(A_i=a\mid U_{i-1}=u,U_i=v)=(1+auv/2)/2\), \(P(T=t\mid A=a,U_0=u)=(1+tb(\prod_i a_i)u)/2\), and \(P(Y=y\mid T=t,U_k=v)=(1+y(\gamma t+\delta v))/2\). Define \(\mathcal M_{1,\pi}\) by \((\gamma,\delta)=(1/8,1/4)\) and \(\mathcal M_{2,\pi}\) by \((\gamma,\delta)=(1/8+c_k/16,1/8)\); vertices and allowed edges outside \(\pi\) use independent full-support mechanisms chosen identically in both models.

definitions.name: Occurrence-consistent selector-isolated compiler
definitions.construction: Given \(\exists X\,\forall Z\,\Phi(X,Z)\) with \(\Phi\) in \(3\)-DNF, form \(F=\neg\Phi\) in \(3\)-CNF; create a pair \(p_o^0,p_o^1\) for every existential-literal occurrence, a budget-saturating pair-test path for each occurrence, two consistency paths for each pair of consecutive copies, and a series composition of selector-isolated clause chains whose surviving \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path represents \(F\). Every module edge is replaced by a private constant-local chain guarded by its selector word and, where appropriate, its universal-literal mode. Set \(B\) equal to the number of existential occurrences and emit the canonical bit string \(\mathbf i\) listing all vertices, fixed and switched edges, guard coordinates, induced equality-or-complement relations, unit costs, terminals, and the binary budget.

definitions.name: Compiled-cut rounding map
definitions.construction: For a budget-feasible vertex set \(K\) in \(\mathcal C(\Phi)\), \(\rho(K)\) replaces every selected selector, clause-chain, consistency-path, or pair-test auxiliary by an unselected occurrence-pair endpoint whose private pair test is exposed, iterating in occurrence order; it keeps selected occurrence endpoints and deletes redundant auxiliaries.
inputs: A budget-feasible vertex set in \(\mathcal C(\Phi)\)

definitions.name: Fixed-completion certificate interface
definitions.construction: Given \(J\), the released exogenous configuration record \(h\), and \(\mathcal S_J\), run breadth-first search in \(H_h-J\). If disconnected, output \(D_h(J)\), \(A_h(J)\), and \(\Psi_{h,J,t,y}\); if connected, output a simple path \(\pi\), its induced \(Y\)-rooted hedge, and the parameter table for \(\mathcal M_{1,\pi},\mathcal M_{2,\pi}\).

definitions.name: Bounded-terminal frontier handle
definitions.construction: Start from \(\mathcal C\) and test degree reduction through private binary splitter interfaces protected by the same budget-saturating pair tests; in parallel, summarize residual path connectivity by boundary signatures indexed by \(d\).

statements.statement: For every fixed \(h\in\mathbb B^R\), \(J\subseteq W\), and simple path \(\pi=(T,A_1,\ldots,A_k,Y)\) in \(H_h-J\), the models \(\mathcal M_{1,\pi}\) and \(\mathcal M_{2,\pi}\) both lie in the same fiber \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\), induce identical completion-indexed information bundles \(\mathcal I_{h,J}=(h,\mathcal S_J)\), and satisfy \(E_{\mathcal M_{2,\pi}}[Y\mid do(T=t)]-E_{\mathcal M_{1,\pi}}[Y\mid do(T=t)]=2^{-k}t/16\).
statements.justification: This proves semantic necessity within the one completion indexed by the released configuration record and never compares models from different fibers.
statements.gap: Kivva et al. construct positive witnesses for general gID but do not give this fixed-completion, path-indexed binary pair matching every cell of one multiplex experiment.
statements.consumer: A dosearch failure report can attach a numerical full-support countermodel pair to a residual-path hedge indexed by the logged configuration.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(h\in\mathbb B^R\) and \(J\subseteq W\), when the exogenous configuration record \(h\) is released as part of \(\mathcal I_{h,J}\) after acquisition, the target \(\theta_t(y)\) is identifiable from \(\mathcal I_{h,J}\) over the single fiber \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\) if and only if \(T\) and \(Y\) are disconnected in \(H_h-J\). When disconnected, for every \(t,y\in\mathbb B\), \(\theta_t(y)=\Psi_{h,J,t,y}(\mathcal I_{h,J})\).
statements.justification: The theorem turns a fixed-completion gID query indexed by recorded configuration metadata into exact separation and an evaluable completion-indexed functional.
statements.gap: Lee et al. and Kivva et al. solve fixed-graph gID generally; the delta is the causal-star iff collapse and explicit strictly positive binary necessity within every fixed completion fiber.
statements.consumer: This is the correctness theorem for a dosearch planner that commissions one source before release of a logged device or site configuration and evaluates it afterward.

statements.statement: For every valid instance string \(\mathbf i\), proxy set \(J\subseteq W\), and completion record \(h\in\mathbb B^R\), \(\mathsf{Ver}(\mathbf i,J,h)\) is computable in time polynomial in \(|\mathbf i|\), equals one if and only if \(J\) satisfies the encoded unit-cost budget and disconnects \(T\) from \(Y\) in \(H_h-J\), and on a connectivity failure returns a simple residual \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path. Consequently, \(\mathbf i\in\mathsf{RSJID}\) if and only if there is a polynomial-length encoding of \(J\) such that \(\mathsf{Ver}(\mathbf i,J,h)=1\) for every polynomial-length \(h\in\mathbb B^R\).
statements.justification: This supplies the explicit polynomial predicate required for the second-level membership argument and a checkable rejecting path.
statements.gap: The causal-design comparators do not formulate this switched robust language as a bit-string language with a fixed-completion separation verifier.
statements.consumer: A QBF backend can compile the predicate directly and expose a path witness for each rejecting universal assignment.

statements.statement: For every \(\Phi\in\operatorname{3DNF}(X,Z)\), the compiler \(\mathcal C\) runs in polynomial time and emits a valid instance string \(\mathbf i=\mathcal C(\Phi)\) of length \(O(L\log L)\) satisfying the encoded unit-cost, singleton-terminal, constant-local-switch, equality-or-complement, and nonterminal-degree-eight restrictions. Its occurrence-pair tests force every budget-\(B\) robust cut to spend exactly one vertex per existential occurrence; its consecutive-copy consistency paths make these choices encode one assignment \(x\in\mathbb B^X\); its universal guards make every switch assignment encode one \(z\in\mathbb B^Z\); and selector isolation ensures that a residual \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path exists exactly when a clause chain for \(\neg\Phi(x,z)\) survives, with no inactive-module bypass. For every auxiliary-inclusive budget-feasible cut \(K\), \(\rho(K)\) is an occurrence-endpoint cut with \(|\rho(K)|\le |K|\) and no weaker completion-wise separation. Consequently, \(\exists X\,\forall Z\,\Phi(X,Z)\) holds if and only if some \(J\subseteq W\) with \(|J|\le B\) disconnects \(T\) and \(Y\) in every \(H_h-J\), equivalently if and only if \(\mathcal C(\Phi)\in\mathsf{RSJID}\).
statements.justification: This isolates all non-routine reduction invariants, including existential proxy choice, universal switching, selector isolation, and rounding away auxiliary interventions.
statements.gap: Bachtler et al. supply a related quantified path-separation skeleton, but their selected arc pairs do not establish these unit-cost proxy-copy and auxiliary-rounding invariants.
statements.consumer: The standalone audit gives a QBF implementation a precise extraction and regression-testing contract.

statements.statement: The explicit bit-string language \(\mathsf{RSJID}\) is \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-complete under polynomial many-one reductions, even with unit proxy costs, singleton \(T\) and \(Y\), constant-size two-mode local switches with equality or complement copies only, binary observed variables, and maximum nonterminal bidirected degree at most eight. Membership is witnessed by a polynomial-length \(J\) and the universal polynomial-time predicate \(\mathsf{Ver}(\mathbf i,J,h)\). For every valid \(\mathbf i\) decoding \((\mathfrak G,B)\), \(\mathbf i\in\mathsf{RSJID}\) if and only if \(\mathcal J_B(\mathfrak G)\ne\varnothing\): under the field-level protocol, \(J\) and \(\mathcal S_J\) are selected before the exogenous configuration record \(h\) is released, and feasibility means that \(\theta_t(y)\) is identifiable over \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\) for every fixed \(h\). Moreover, \(\exists X\,\forall Z\,\Phi(X,Z)\) if and only if \(\mathcal C(\Phi)\in\mathsf{RSJID}\).
statements.justification: It isolates a quantified complexity jump caused by committing to one experiment before correlated local graph modes are learned.
statements.gap: Akbari et al. and Elahi et al. study one known ADMG, while Bachtler et al. select forbidden arc pairs in a fixed graph; none proves this recorded-configuration causal vertex-intervention language under the restriction package.
statements.consumer: A dosearch planner can justify a QBF backend while retaining completion-specific gID semantics after release of the logged configuration record.

statements.statement: For any supplied \(J\), released exogenous configuration record \(h\), and source \(\mathcal S_J\), the certificate interface runs in time polynomial in \(|V|+|E_h^{\leftrightarrow}|\). It returns \(D_h(J)\), \(A_h(J)\), and \(\Psi_{h,J,t,y}\) when identification holds over \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\); otherwise it returns a simple path, its completion-specific \(Y\)-rooted hedge, and two same-fiber positive binary countermodels. Thus a robust \(J\) admits one polynomially checkable gID certificate per queried configuration, whereas a fixed failing \(J\) admits a configuration-plus-hedge witness.
statements.justification: Both success and failure are checked relative to the fixed completion indexed by the same logged record that indexes the identifying functional.
statements.gap: Fixed-graph gID and PAG algorithms provide local proof objects, but the local-switch design literature lacks this fiber-correct two-sided interface.
statements.consumer: The objects feed directly into a dosearch pre-data design report and a QBF counterexample viewer.

statements.statement: If \(R=\varnothing\), minimizing \(|J|\) over \(\mathcal J_B(\mathfrak G)\) is exactly the minimum internal \(T\)-to-\(Y\) vertex-cut problem in the fixed bidirected graph and is solvable in polynomial time by vertex splitting and maximum flow.
statements.justification: This locates hardness in the ex ante universal completion quantifier rather than a hidden fixed-graph causal obstruction.
statements.gap: Known-graph intervention design is generally NP-complete, but the causal-star subclass collapses to ordinary minimum cut.
statements.consumer: The planner can dispatch single-completion stars to maximum flow.

statements.statement: If there exists \(h^*\in\mathbb B^R\) such that \(E_h^{\leftrightarrow}\subseteq E_{h^*}^{\leftrightarrow}\) for every \(h\), then \(J\in\mathcal J_B(\mathfrak G)\) if and only if \(J\) disconnects \(T\) and \(Y\) in \(H_{h^*}-J\); equivalently, identification in the fixed fiber at \(h^*\) certifies identification in every fixed fiber.
statements.justification: Complementary correlations, rather than uncertainty with a largest completion, cause the quantified hardness.
statements.gap: Robust-flow models often admit a worst scenario; this proposition identifies the exact collapse for the present completion-indexed source protocol.
statements.consumer: A planner can replace robust search by one minimum cut whenever a greatest completion exists.

statements.statement: Characterize the exact complexity of \(\mathsf{RSJID}\) when every completion has bidirected degree at most \(d\) at both \(T\) and \(Y\), while the union of possible switched neighborhoods may be unbounded: determine whether a fixed \(d\) preserves \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-completeness or yields a polynomial-time or fixed-parameter algorithm.
statements.justification: The lower bound controls nonterminal degree but leaves both terminal degrees unbounded.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash show that fixed-graph structure can restore tractability, while Bachtler et al.'s acyclic hardness does not control terminal incidence.
statements.consumer: The frontier determines whether sparse completion-wise terminal neighborhoods admit a specialized exact dosearch planner.

sampling_model.design: Choose one unit-cost set \(J\subseteq W\) and acquire every \(Q_{J,j}\) before access to \(h\). The acquisition system then releases the already logged exogenous device or site configuration bits \(h\); the prespecified guard map \(\lambda\) maps that record to \(G_h\), and \((h,\mathcal S_J)\) is available before target evaluation.
sampling_model.units: For each recorded \(h\), identification is evaluated within the strictly positive binary recursive semi-Markovian fiber \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\); the protocol does not estimate bidirected edges from \(P\), from the interventional laws, or from manifestations of latent confounding, and models from different completions are never pooled.
sampling_model.treatment: The singleton treatment is \(T\), and interventions on \(T\) or \(Y\) are infeasible.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of \(P\) makes every conditional in the completion-indexed adjustment functional well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; finite-sample estimation is outside the theorem kernel.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The edge-ID problem is NP-complete for selecting a plausible identifiable subgraph under probabilistic edge uncertainty.
Minimum-cost intervention design on one known semi-Markovian graph is NP-complete and equivalent to hitting relevant hedges.
A Boolean reachability construction yields weighted MAX-SAT and integer-programming formulations for fixed-graph proxy design.
Under positivity, a target district is g-identifiable if and only if it is classically identifiable in at least one supplied source graph.
The gID algorithm is sound and complete on a fixed graph with arbitrary surrogate experiments.
CIDP and its calculus are complete for conditional-effect identification from a PAG.
Separating by forbidden pairs is \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-complete even on acyclic graphs.
Minimum-cardinality interdiction is \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-complete for a broad list of nominal problems admitting invulnerability reductions.
Robust minimum cut and adaptive network-flow variants under structural failures are NP-hard.
The two-stage stochastic minimum cut problem is NP-hard in general and polynomial-time solvable on trees.

tldr: One multiplex proxy experiment is selected before release of exogenous device or site configuration bits that, through a prespecified guard map, determine the fixed graph completion used at evaluation. Within each fixed positive-binary causal-star fiber, the source and logged configuration identify \(\theta_t(y)\) exactly when deleting the intervention vertices disconnects \(T\) from \(Y\); the positive direction has a completion-indexed adjustment functional and every surviving path has same-fiber full-support binary countermodels. The resulting explicit bit-string design language has a polynomial fixed-completion verifier and is \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-complete under the stated local-switch restrictions.

project_justification.gap: Existing gID algorithms condition on one fixed graph, existing proxy-design algorithms optimize for one known ADMG, and uncertain-network work uses different criteria. None couples ex ante acquisition with later release of recorded exogenous configuration metadata over explicitly separated fixed-completion fibers or formulates the resulting robust decision problem as an auditable bit-string language.
project_justification.niche: The niche is one proxy set valid for every member of a succinct family whose optional bidirected edges share equality or complement switch bits, while the evaluator may use the realized graph and its completion-indexed functional.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a fixed-fiber positive-binary star iff theorem, an explicit polynomial fixed-completion verifier, a standalone occurrence and selector compiler audit establishing quantified hardness, and a certificate interface returning completion-indexed adjustment districts or same-fiber hedge countermodels.

related_work: Akbari et al. (2023) make graph uncertainty central but optimize the probability of an identifiable subgraph rather than one experiment valid for every completion indexed by subsequently released exogenous configuration metadata. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025) prove NP-completeness and hedge hitting for minimum-cost design on one known graph; their machinery informs the intervention side. Elahi et al. (2024) encode fixed-graph proxy design as weighted MAX-SAT and integer programming; the present compiler adds universal switches, occurrence consistency, selector isolation, and an auxiliary-cut rounding map. Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (2020) give fixed-graph gID formulas and thicket witnesses, and Kivva et al. (2022) repair gID under positivity; these works inform the fixed-completion fiber theorem rather than identification over a union of graph classes. Jaber et al. (2022) prove completeness over a PAG, but a PAG does not preserve arbitrary equality or complement correlations. Bachtler, Bergner, and Krumke (2024) establish the closest quantified path-separation result, while Grüne and Wulf (2026) give a broad blocking framework; neither supplies the causal source semantics, the explicit encoded verifier, or the proxy-vertex rounding lemma. Bertsimas, Nasrabadi, and Stiller (2013) and Rebennack, Prokopyev, and Singh (2020) study robust or recourse cuts under different uncertainty and timing semantics.
technical_internal_limitation: The compiler audit remains a proof obligation: bounded checks support, but do not replace, the uniform arguments for occurrence bookkeeping, selector isolation, and the rounding map. Exact dyadic checks for paths with zero through four internal proxies support, but do not replace, the symbolic same-fiber induction. Terminal degrees remain unbounded.
honest_scope: Identification is always asserted within a fixed fiber \(\mathcal P_{+,h}(G_h,J)\) after the directly logged exogenous configuration record \(h\) is released with \(\mathcal S_J\); latent bidirected edges are not inferred from the acquired laws. No identification claim is made over an unindexed union of completions or for a formula chosen before metadata release. The result is restricted to directed causal stars and strictly positive binary models. The complexity theorem bounds nonterminal bidirected degree but not terminal degree. No claim is made for PAG families, unrestricted strictly binary gID completeness, finite-sample estimation, or polynomial-time discovery of a failing completion. With \(R=\varnothing\) the design problem is ordinary minimum vertex cut; a greatest completion suffices when present; and if \(A_h(J)=\varnothing\), the functional reduces to \(Q_{J,j_0}(Y=y\mid T=t)\).

seed_details.rebuttal: The exact star reduction and binary same-source pair are unstated.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The class is a fixed completion fiber rather than a union.

seed_details.seed: Two-sided switch-aware certification without completion enumeration
seed_details.opportunity: Return a per-completion formula or a fixed failing completion and hedge.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compress fixed-graph gID output to a district or residual path.
seed_details.target_method_search: No switch-correlation-aware certificate interface was located.
seed_details.red_team: Breadth-first search is routine once \(h\) is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is an operational consequence, not the standalone headline.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Every output is indexed by the fixed completion determined by the logged configuration record.

seed_details.opportunity: Resolve complexity under bounded completion-wise terminal degree.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace terminal hubs by protected splitter interfaces.
seed_details.red_team: Bounded degree may trivialize the candidate neighborhood.
seed_details.rebuttal: The switched union may remain unbounded.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Posed only as an open-ended question with a concrete handle.

seed_details.seed: QBF compilation with intervention-safe auxiliary vertices
seed_details.opportunity: Give a quantified encoding with extractable causal witnesses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Add universal guards, pair tests, selector isolation, and rounding.
seed_details.target_method_search: Fixed-graph SAT encodings do not provide these quantified invariants.
seed_details.red_team: Replacing SAT by QBF may be routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Auxiliary cuts and module bypasses make the compiler audit non-routine.

seed_details.seed: Fixed-design robustness and its coNP boundary
seed_details.opportunity: Classify verification of a supplied design.
seed_details.target_method_search: No causal fixed-design classification was located.
seed_details.red_team: It is only the universal half of the main reduction.
seed_details.rebuttal: Accordingly it is not a standalone theorem here.

seed_details.opportunity: Develop a complete calculus for correlated switched ADMG families.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Carry Boolean guards through graphical rules.
seed_details.target_method_search: No such complete calculus was located.
seed_details.rebuttal: Succinctness matters, but this exceeds the star kernel.

seed_details.seed: One formula valid before completion revelation
seed_details.target_method_search: No result for arbitrary equality or complement switch circuits was located.
seed_details.rebuttal: The protocol releases the exogenous record \(h\) before evaluation, so this stronger object is excluded.

seed_details.opportunity: Recognize greatest completions and study bounded interfaces.
seed_details.target_method_search: No causal switch-width theorem was located.
seed_details.red_team: A greatest completion makes the cut immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is retained only as a sanity reduction.

chosen_threads.candidate: Quantified robust joint-proxy design on locally switched causal stars
chosen_threads.settled: Forbidden-pair separation has second-level hardness; known-graph causal design is NP-complete and has SAT or ILP formulations.
chosen_threads.unoccupied_pair: No located result combines fixed ex ante multiplex acquisition, later release of logged exogenous switch metadata, correlated local switches, binary star semantics, and auxiliary-safe vertex deletion.
chosen_threads.closest_subsumption_check: The combinatorial papers lack the causal fixed-fiber semantics and proxy rounding obligations.

chosen_threads.candidate: Exact positive-binary source criterion for a fixed causal-star completion
chosen_threads.settled: Positive gID and arbitrary surrogate-experiment gID are complete on one fixed graph.
chosen_threads.unoccupied_pair: The residual-path iff theorem and explicit same-fiber binary pair are unstated.
chosen_threads.closest_subsumption_check: General gID informs sufficiency but does not state the star functional or binary construction.

chosen_threads.settled: Fixed-graph and PAG procedures return local proof objects.
chosen_threads.unoccupied_pair: No located interface preserves equality or complement switch correlations while returning per-completion certificates.
chosen_threads.closest_subsumption_check: PAGs do not encode the required cross-edge Boolean correlations.
